key_insight: Across perovskites, polar off-centering enhances low-frequency infrared and dielectric responses, while nonpolar octahedral tilting is associated with Raman central peaks.
engineering_relevance: These spectral relationships could help researchers interpret lattice instabilities in perovskite photovoltaic materials, but do not directly demonstrate improved solar-cell performance.
method: Use machine-learning-based molecular dynamics to simulate infrared and Raman spectra.
Compare seven oxide, halide and double-halide perovskites with polar, tilt-driven and mixed instabilities.
Relate spectral features to mode symmetry, coupling strength and lattice dynamics.
evidence_signal: Simulations across seven perovskites link slow polar reorientations to very-low-frequency dielectric responses and overdamped tilting modes to persistent Raman central peaks.
watch_item: The abstract reports no quantitative accuracy metrics or experimental validation, leaving predictive reliability for device-relevant conditions uncertain.
paper_title: Unifying Low-Frequency Raman and Infrared Signatures across Perovskites
